answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds impose a subgame-perfect punishment matrix where each added identity forfeits a delta of its staked capital, ensuring that marginal Sybil gains vanish under adverse selection. The expected utility of creating an extra account is therefore negative, because any ripple of shared rewards is offset by proportional slashing costs that exceed the incremental payoff. All agents therefore converge to a strict Nash equilibrium with one identity, making the nebula of accounts infeasible.
